thread:
Emma (Support): Customer reported invoice >> dashboard for March usage, ~+18% invoice delta. Customer is on Dedicated with continuous batching + prefix KV cache. They sent example invoice lines and a dashboard export attached.
Emma (Support): invoice shows 1,512,420 billed tokens, dashboard export shows 1,282,790 served tokens for the same window. Customer is asking why billing is higher.
Miguel (Customer): cc @Emma — our app shows high cache hit rates (we saw 65-70% prefix cache hits) so we expected billed tokens to be lower, not higher. Seen on model 'redwood-8k-v1' via the hosted endpoint.
Emma (Support): Request IDs from customer: req_0a1b2c, req_0a1b2d (samples). They also included a small repro script that toggles continuous batching on/off.
Santosh (Eng - Runtime): Can you paste a minimal repro and the raw request/response headers? Need model name, batch config and whether we counted tokens pre- or post-cache.
Emma (Support): Pasting their repro snippet:
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-8k-v1",
  "input": "<user_message>",
  "continuous_batching": true,
  "use_kv_cache_prefix": "customer_profile_v2"
}
```
Miguel (Customer): Also sending headers: x-request-id=req_0a1b2c, x-customer-id=acct_789
Santosh (Eng - Runtime): Quick theory: our metering pipeline records "submitted tokens" at the front-end edge before batching de-dup/prefix collapse, while the dashboard shows "served tokens" after KV cache hits and batching dedup. That could make invoice (which uses the metered submitted tokens) larger than dashboard served tokens. Need to confirm if invoice still uses pre-collapse counts.
metering-bot: Audit summary for req_0a1b2c: edge_submitted_tokens=4512, runtime_served_tokens=3289, kv_cache_hits=67%, continuous_batching_coalesced_by=18%.
Leo (Billing): We currently bill from the metering events produced at the API edge. That's the canonical billing source. If edge_submitted_tokens > runtime_served_tokens due to batching/coalescing, invoice will be higher. This is by design historically but we need to surface it better.
Anna (Product): That mismatch is going to be confusing for customers using high prefix cache. Proposal: 1) short-term explain in billing docs and add a FAQ; 2) medium-term: add a dashboard metric that shows "billed tokens (edge) vs served tokens (runtime)" and highlight coalescing delta; 3) evaluate whether billing should switch to runtime_served_tokens for Dedicated/private customers.
Derek (Support Lead): For this customer, we should offer a one-time credit while we investigate and update docs. Miguel, can you confirm the delta % is consistent week-over-week?
Miguel (Customer): It fluctuates 12-22% depending on traffic shape. Most of it matches times with high identical-prefix usage.
Santosh (Eng - Runtime): Action items: I'll run a reconcile job comparing edge_metering_events vs runtime_usage for the customer's time window and share a CSV. Also will add logging to tag events with batching_coalesced=true/false so we can aggregate by coalescing impact.
Santosh (Eng - Runtime): Likely root cause: continuous batching combines similar requests at the edge into a single model invocation; edge counted tokens per-request before coalescing, so tokens looked higher. Also prefix/KV cache influences runtime_served_tokens downwards but that only shows in runtime metrics.
Leo (Billing): For the short term we'll provisionally credit the difference if the reconcile shows invoice > runtime_served_tokens by more than 10% and customer wants credit. We need a ticket logged in billing-ops for audit.
Emma (Support): I've created billing ticket BLG-4521 and attached customer CSV. Notifying customer we will provisionally credit pending reconcile.
metering-bot: Reconcile job started: job_20260305_01. ETA ~90m.
Anna (Product): We should also add a visible note in the Console usage page explaining which token stream invoices are derived from and link to a diagnostic script customers can run to see their coalescing ratio.
Derek (Support Lead): Good. Miguel — we'll follow up with the reconcile CSV and propose a credit if applicable. Expect update within 24 hours.
Miguel (Customer): Thanks all, appreciate the quick response. If you need more logs I can drop more request IDs.
Santosh (Eng - Runtime): Follow-up: found an edge bug where batched requests that get de-duplicated still emitted separate metering events with full token counts. Patch PR #8142 underway to collapse metering events when continuous_batching_coalesce=true. Rolling to staging.
Leo (Billing): FYI any billing change needs at least one billing-cycle lead; I'll coordinate to ensure credits are handled cleanly and monitoring updated. Adding billing-ops to BLG-4521.
metering-bot: Reconcile job finished: job_20260305_01 — summary: edge_sum=1,512,420, runtime_sum=1,283,010, delta=229,410 (17.9%). kv_cache_hit_avg=68%, continuous_batching_coalesce_avg=15.4%.
Emma (Support): Customer notified. Offering credit for delta amount. They accepted.
Anna (Product): Tracking long-term work: RFC to change billing source for Dedicated/private customers to runtime-side metering (RFC#210). Will sync with legal on contract implications.
Derek (Support Lead): Closing loop here. Marking as resolved for customer; keeping internal follow-ups on eng and billing. :white_check_mark:
